review: 702.111b-1: variant one_creature_only did not flip the outcome (still illegal, like the base); replaced it with no_menace (attacker is vanilla Hill Giant, single block legal).

scenarios.title: A creature with menace can be blocked only by two or more creatures

setup.notes: Boggart Brute (3/2 menace) has been declared as an attacker against B and the declare blockers step has begun. B's two Grizzly Bears are untapped.

decisions: A attacks B with Boggart Brute in the declare attackers step.
B proposes to block Boggart Brute with exactly one Grizzly Bears and declares no other blocker; the engine's verdict on that block declaration is read.

variants.label: single_blocker
variants.expected: The block declaration is illegal: Boggart Brute cannot be blocked by only one creature, so a lone Grizzly Bears is rejected as its blocker.

variants.label: two_blockers
variants.delta: B declares both Grizzly Bears as blockers of Boggart Brute instead of one.
variants.expected: The block declaration is legal: Boggart Brute is blocked by both Grizzly Bears.

variants.label: no_menace
variants.delta: A's attacker is Hill Giant (3/3, no menace) instead of Boggart Brute.
variants.expected: The block declaration is legal: Hill Giant is blocked by the single Grizzly Bears.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge enforces menace when validating the whole block declaration, so each blocker alone looks like a legal blocker individually while the combined declaration is rejected.
